author: WP13
summary: Updated chapter on the two skeletal systems, SkinningData/AnimationPlayer validation, the three skin index spaces, the D8 root prefix, clip resampling, scaling limits and frame order. Current in substance; TARGET adds load-time bind-pose palettes, explicit scene/palette maps, the half-open STEP rule, refusal of skins over 72 joints, rigid-clip target spaces and shared keyframe aliases. Tutorials 112/113 held the user-level API; the D8 derivation, index-space model, validation edges and prefix rationale now live on the skinning deep dive, and the avatar path is already covered by the avatars deep dive.

concepts.section: Skinning and Animation across Two Systems
concepts.text: CNA has two skeletal systems that deliberately do not share a runtime graph: SkinningData plus AnimationPlayer animate an ordinary Model; SkinnedModelEXT is an Avatar-oriented model, skeleton, clip and draw system.
tokens: do not share a runtime graph

concepts.section: Skinning and Animation across Two Systems
concepts.text: Similar interpolation code appears in both; the duplicated SampleTrack is documented as intentional because forcing the public types together would couple two asset contracts.

concepts.section: Skinning and Animation across Two Systems
concepts.text: The two systems do share keyframe vocabulary: Keyframe and AnimationClip are aliases of KeyframeEXT and AnimationClipEXT.
tokens: Keyframe and AnimationClip are using aliases
concepts.note: Adds the shared alias types the claim does not mention.

concepts.text: A skinned Model carries SkinningData through Model::Tag with bind-pose locals, inverse binds, parent indices, clips and a fourth array SkeletonRootPrefix.
SkinningData also carries SkeletonRootNodeIndexEXT and SkeletonRootNameEXT, the rig root named by skin.skeleton, for locating the rig; they influence no transform by design.
Multiple skins: getSkinsEXTProperty lists each skin's SkinningData and meshes; animate each with its own player and install its palette only on its meshes.
tokens: install its palette only on its own meshes

concepts.text: AnimationPlayer samples a clip into locals, composes worlds in topological order and builds the skin palette for SkinnedEffect or SkinnedPbrEffect.
The player keeps a pointer to SkinningData (which must outlive it) and to the started clip; construction computes the bind pose immediately.
Update adds or seeks; looping reduces the position modulo duration on raw ticks with floor-mod for negatives; non-looping clamps to [0, Duration]; no clip or zero duration holds at zero.
Model::Draw sets IEffectMatrices world per mesh but never installs a bone palette; the application must call SetBoneTransforms, and a non-IEffectMatrices effect is rejected.
Model::CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo is not a palette: it is indexed by scene node and contains no inverse binds.
A skinned effect's palette defaults to identity matrices, meaning every joint matrix is identity, so an unanimated glTF skin renders wrong; readers call ApplyBindPoseBoneTransformsEXT at load.
concepts.note: Adds the load-time bind-pose palette at TARGET.

concepts.text: ApplyBindPoseBoneTransformsEXT poses only meshes mapped to that skin when SkinsEXT exists, all skinned effects otherwise, returns the number posed and holds no state.
tokens: returns the number of effects posed

concepts.text: Loaded effects are shared across copies and cached loads, so two characters drawn from one model must each install their palette immediately before their own draw.
SkinnedModelEXT is not built from ModelBone/ModelMesh/ModelMeshPart, owns its Avatar geometry and animation and loads from .skinnedmodel.json.
concepts.note: Covered by the avatars deep dive (SkinnedModelEXT contract and content format).

concepts.text: Its SampleTrack logic is a local copy, not a hidden conversion to AnimationPlayer.

Both players require bone arrays to agree in size (ArgumentException) and each non-root parent index to precede its child; a parent >= current index throws, which also rejects self-parenting and cycles.
tokens: which also rejects self-parenting and cycles

concepts.text: Any negative parent value means root, not only -1; tracks with empty keys or out-of-range bone indices are silently ignored.
Translations and scales interpolate linearly and rotations spherically; track search is linear in keyframes per bone.
tokens: linear search for the bracketing key

concepts.text: AnimationPlayer's constructor casts BoneCount to size_t for its vectors before the size check, so a negative count requests an enormous allocation instead of the later ArgumentException; validate custom SkinningData first.
Content readers reject implausible bone counts: the .cnj skeleton accepts 0 to 100,000 and glTF skins are capped at 72 joints.

concepts.section: Scene indices are not palette indices
concepts.text: The glTF scene is flattened into ModelBone indices while a skin's joints array defines a separate list that need not be parent-before-child.

concepts.section: Scene indices are not palette indices
concepts.text: BuildSkeleton reorders joints breadth-first into topological order, records old-to-new, and rewrites packed JOINTS_0 through it; unresolved parent chains and duplicate joints are refused.

concepts.section: Scene indices are not palette indices
concepts.text: Three indices must be kept apart: scene-node index (placement, rigid clips, cameras), source-joint ordinal (JOINTS_0), and palette index (SkinningData arrays, skeletal tracks, effect palette).

concepts.section: Scene indices are not palette indices
concepts.text: SkeletonResult carries sceneNodeIndexToPaletteIndex and paletteIndexToSceneNodeIndex because the scene graph must never be reordered to make spaces coincide.

concepts.section: Scene indices are not palette indices
concepts.text: Treating any two index spaces as interchangeable works only on conveniently authored fixtures; reversed-joint-order tests rule that out.

concepts.section: The coordinate-space failure that produced D8
concepts.text: Older logic walked joint parents only within the joint set, dropping the armature's world transform while keeping inverse binds that encoded it, so a uniformly scaled armature collapsed toward the origin (D8).

concepts.section: The coordinate-space failure that produced D8
concepts.text: The corrected root term is P_root = W_ancestor * inverse(W_meshNode): ancestry above the joint set, times cancellation of the node instancing the skinned mesh.

concepts.section: The coordinate-space failure that produced D8
concepts.text: The cancellation is needed because the skinned mesh is parented to the synthetic root rather than its node.
tokens: glTF requires because the mesh is placed by its joints

concepts.section: The coordinate-space failure that produced D8
concepts.text: The ancestry walk does not stop at skin.skeleton (stopping there reproduces D8), and a joint off a node outside the selected scene gets its ancestry via cgltf's world-transform calculation.

concepts.section: Why the prefix must remain separate
concepts.text: Folding P_root into the root's bind-pose local fails as soon as an animation channel replaces that local transform.

concepts.section: Why the prefix must remain separate
concepts.text: CNA stores one prefix per root in SkeletonRootPrefix and composes W_root(t) = L_root(t) * P_root, so an animated root substitutes only its own local.

concepts.section: Why the prefix must remain separate
concepts.text: The prefix is applied only when the array has exactly BoneCount entries; an empty or mismatched array reads as identity, keeping older CNJ skeleton sidecars valid.
concepts.note: Any size mismatch, not only an empty array, reads as identity.

concepts.section: Why the prefix must remain separate
concepts.text: The skin-mesh-node-transform fixture makes missing, once-applied and twice-applied cancellation numerically distinct (0, -50, -100); the test expects -50 and checks the node bone keeps +50 and the mesh hangs off bone 0.

concepts.section: Why the prefix must remain separate
concepts.text: RootJointCarriesTheSceneAncestryAboveTheJointSet covers the ancestry half on skin-armature-ancestor.
Skeletal clips resample each bone onto the union of its translation, rotation and scale key times, deduplicated at 1e-9, with missing channels falling back to the decomposed bind pose.
STEP holds the value at the start of the half-open interval; an older version returned the previous key at exact boundaries, which after union resampling made a three-key STEP channel play 0, 0, 20.
CUBICSPLINE uses the Hermite basis with tangents scaled by the interval length; cubic rotations are renormalised during sampling.
Baked keyframes keep no interpolation mode or tangents; the player then interpolates linearly, so a cubic channel is exact only at union times.
Clip duration is the largest sampler input time.
Only channels resolving through the skin's joint map enter a skeletal clip; rigid node TRS animation goes through the same resampling as scene-node clips.
Each clip records its index space in AnimationClipEXT::TargetSpace (JointPalette or SceneNode).
On an unskinned model Tag carries ModelAnimationsEXT; ApplyClipToBonesEXT clamps time, writes only tracked bones and throws std::invalid_argument for a palette clip.
A skinned model's Tag is occupied, so rigid tracks not carried by any retained skin are counted and reported as rigid-animation-dropped-on-skinned-model (D6 fixed for the rigid-model route).
Channels targeting nodes outside the selected scene and unsupported paths are counted and reported.

Morph-weight animation locates a weights channel on the first node (in file node order) instancing the mesh, keeps cubic tangents unbaked and evaluates Hermite lazily; if a mesh has several placements, every placement plays that node's track.
tokens: every placement of a mesh instanced by several nodes plays that node's track

concepts.text: Morph position/normal/tangent deltas are CPU-blended into vertex bytes and uploaded again; this is not GPU morphing.
Initial morph weights are the instancing node's weights when present, else the mesh's; non-zero defaults are blended at load and the bounding sphere reflects that pose.
The converter's unitScale applies to every translation-bearing quantity including animation translations and their cubic tangents, never to rotation or scale channels; runtime import fixes it at 1.0.
tokens: never to rotation or scale channels

concepts.text: Both stock skinned effects accept at most 72 palette matrices; each vertex has four byte joint indices and four weights.
A glTF skin over 72 joints is refused at import with its joint count named (skin-73-joints), because truncation would collapse its vertices; larger rigs must be split before import.
concepts.note: The claim said parsing may succeed and drawing fail; TARGET refuses at import.

concepts.text: Frame order: sample the clip, compose worlds with root prefixes, form skin matrices, install each palette on its effects, apply rigid clips, upload changed morph weights, then Model::Draw on the graphics thread.
concepts.note: Adds the rigid-clip step that TARGET supports.

concepts.text: The thread-local draw scratch removed a cross-thread race, but graphics resources and the shared model graph are not thread-safe; keep animation and drawing under graphics-thread ownership.

figures.note: Redrawn at TARGET with the explicit scene-node/palette maps (sceneNodeIndexToPaletteIndex, paletteIndexToSceneNodeIndex) that the import core now carries, the 72-matrix palette bound and the skin-matrix formula.

issues.text: AnimationPlayer's constructor sizes vectors from static_cast<size_t>(BoneCount) before RecomputeTransforms validates sizes, so a negative BoneCount in hand-built SkinningData yields an allocation failure instead of ArgumentException.
Morph weight tracks use the first node in file order that instances a mesh; every placement of a multi-placed mesh plays that node's track (documented simplification).
A skinned model cannot also carry rigid scene-node clips; extra rigid tracks are dropped with a named report diagnostic (GLTF-295).
glTF skins with more than 72 joints are refused at import; cubic bone channels are baked to keys and played back linearly between them.
